proposal: The Mandate argues that the Conservation Reserve Program pays farmers not to farm a large share of their land and recommends that the next Administration champion eliminating it, with USDA working with Congress. It says any need to keep very sensitive land out of production should be met through targeted efforts tied to a specific, concrete environmental harm.
remaining: Elimination of CRP by statute (p. 304): no bill or administration proposal to end it was found, and the committee-reported farm bill would reauthorize it.

status_summary: USDA has continued to run the program. On 2026-02-10 it opened 2026 continuous and general signups, noting that CRP was close to its 27-million-acre statutory cap with about 1.9 million acres available for the fiscal year, and on 2026-07-07 it announced acceptance of 2.2 million acres out of about 2.5 million acres offered across the general, grassland and continuous signups. The House Agriculture Committee advanced the Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026 (H.R. 7567) by a 34-17 vote in early March 2026, and Quail Forever reports that it reauthorizes CRP through 2031. A CRS primer dated 2026-04-13 says CRP's authority has run on short extensions since the end of FY2023 and was extended through FY2026, and that without authority CRP could not enroll new or expiring acres. No proposal from USDA or Congress to eliminate CRP, and no targeted replacement program, was found.

timeline.event: USDA announces 2026 enrollment: continuous CRP (Signup 65) from 2026-02-12 to 2026-03-20 and general CRP (Signup 66) from 2026-03-09 to 2026-04-17, with CRP near its 27-million-acre cap and about 1.9 million acres available; the release says FSA's authority to run CRP was extended through 2026-09-30.

Quail Forever reports (publication date; the markup was the week before) that the House Agriculture Committee advanced the Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026 by 34-17 with all Republicans and seven Democrats in favor, and that the bill reauthorizes CRP through 2031.

CRS Farm Bill Primer on the conservation title states that CRP has a 27-million-acre cap for FY2026, that its authority was extended through FY2026 and is the largest conservation program set to expire then, that CBO puts outlays near $2.0 billion a year, and that the House Agriculture Committee ordered H.R. 7567 reported.

USDA announces it accepted 2.2 million acres into CRP for 2026 from about 2.5 million acres offered, with Nebraska, Colorado and South Dakota receiving the most; an FSA official credits voluntary, producer-led conservation.

title: Eliminate the Conservation Reserve Program and rely on targeted conservation instead
uncertainties: The farm bill's CRP text was not read: the reauthorization through 2031 comes from an advocacy group's summary (Quail Forever), and the CRS primer did not describe H.R. 7567's CRP provisions. The committee markup date is given only as the week before 2026-03-12. Whether the farm bill passed the House or Senate, and whether CRP authority was extended past 2026-09-30 (Public Law 119-103's agriculture extensions, as read, do not name CRP), was not established. The administration's FY2027 budget request for CRP was not checked, and a Federal Register search for the program since 2025-01-20 returned no CRP-specific rule. The FSA program page did not state an authorization end date. The two FSA release titles are descriptive labels written for this record from the page content.
